- Intro: both solve different problems: observer pattern behavioral decoupling, B-tree data structure for storage/retrieval.

Observer Pattern:
- Definition: subject maintains list observers, notifies on state changes.
- Components: Subject, Observer, ConcreteSubject, ConcreteObserver.
- Workflow: observers register; state change triggers notify; each observer update; push/pull.
- Complexity: attach/detach O(1) with hash set; notify O(n); memory O(n). If update methods expensive, total O(n * cost). Need avoid synchronous notification causing latency.
- When choose: one-to-many dynamic dependencies, event-driven UI, MVC, distributed event systems. Alternatives: polling (wasteful), callbacks (tight coupling), pub/sub message queue (decoupled, async, more infrastructure), reactive streams (backpressure). Choose observer for in-process decoupling; choose broker for cross-service.

B-trees:
- Definition: balanced multi-way tree, nodes with sorted keys and child pointers; leaves at same depth.
- How works: order m; each node up to m-1 keys, m children; search starts root, compares keys, descends; insertion search leaf, insert, split if overflow; deletion borrow/merge; height O(log_m n).
- Complexity: search/insert/delete O(log n) worst-case, but in disk terms O(log_m n) I/O; space O(n). With high fanout, height small; e.g. 1 billion keys with 1000 fanout height ~3.
- When choose: databases, filesystems, sorted range queries, sequential access. Alternatives: hash table for exact lookup O(1) but no range; AVL/red-black
